name: Матовий майстер: остання горизонталь (1)
description:
Good chess players are very good in spotting mating patterns. The back-rank mate is a mate that is very common when there is little material left on the board.

Study the examples to see how it works.  

Real mate monster are always on the lookout for a back-rank mate opportunity.

What do you have to do?

Checkmate the king on the back rank. This may take you three or four moves, so keep calculating! If you can move two rooks to the back rank, make sure to pick the safe way. Keep in mind that you may have to give up a piece to checkmate.

examples.text:
The black king is trapped behind the three pawns.
The king cannot move away from the 8th rank, the back rank.
Black can’t take the rook, either.
Nor can he put another piece between the king and the rook (interposing).
It is checkmate, back-rank mate!

White has two options. Both rooks can check the black king.
The smart thing to do is to follow the green arrow. Can you tell why?

Checking the king with the other rook (red arrow) would leave this rook unprotected.
Black can easily get out of check: his queen will take your rook.
What’s more, this also prevents your other rook from checkmating the king.
For the queen is in a good spot to take that rook as well.

In order to checkmate, White needs to give up a piece first.
The black bishop protects the mating square. Yet, this does not save Black.
White has two attackers (the rooks) and Black has only one defender (the bishop).
White starts with the first rook. It checks the king.
The black bishop must capture the white rook. Then the remaining white rook captures the bishop and … back-rank mate.
Black has gained more points in the exchanges, but that does not help him now the game is over.
